name: H01 htmlCommentOpenAt: never reads again from the top
why: a line before the one last asked answers the state of the later one: the named re-read row and the descending and zigzag orders of every enumeration

name: H02 htmlCommentOpenAt: reads again from the top when the same line is asked twice
why: no answer changes, so cost tells it: the production caller never asks one line twice, and the repeated-ask clock row (2,000 asks of the last line of 20,000) fails when a line equal to the last one reads again from the top

name: H03 htmlCommentOpenAt: the re-read keeps the comment state
why: an earlier line asked after a later one inherits the later state: the descending and zigzag orders of every enumeration and the named re-read row

name: H04 htmlCommentOpenAt: the re-read keeps its place
why: the earlier line is never read again, so its answer is false whatever it holds: the named re-read row and the descending order

name: H05 htmlCommentOpenAt: a line past the end is read as far as asked
why: lines[scanned] is undefined past the end and its length is read: the past-the-end rows and the enumerations' last two lines

name: H06 htmlCommentOpenAt: reads the line asked about as well
why: a comment opened or closed ON the line asked is counted: the closing-line row and the enumerations

name: H07 htmlCommentOpenAt: skips every second line
why: the enumerations and the multi-line rows

name: H08 htmlCommentOpenAt: the closer is searched from the line's start
why: a closer before the opener on one line closes it again and again: the loop never ends when text follows the opener (`--><!--x`, `a --> b <!-- c`; the line `--><!--` alone ends): killed by timeout (run this list with --timeout 60, not the default 600)

name: H09 htmlCommentOpenAt: steps over four after a closer and three after an opener
why: `<!--->` reads differently (three after an opener finds the closer in its own dashes: the named row and the enumerations) and so does `--><!--` (four after a closer skips the `<` of the opener that follows it); `<!-->` reads the same

name: H10 htmlCommentOpenAt: steps over four after a closer too
why: four after a closer skips the character right after it, the `<` of an opener that begins there (`--><!--`): the token and the line-list enumerations

name: H11 htmlCommentOpenAt: steps over three after an opener too
why: `<!--->` closes at once: the named row and the character enumeration

name: H12 htmlCommentOpenAt: every marker opens
why: a closer never closes: the closed-comment rows and the enumerations

name: H13 htmlCommentOpenAt: starts with a comment open
why: line 0 answers open: the named row and every enumeration

name: H14 htmlCommentOpenAt: starts reading at the second line
why: a comment opened on the first line is never seen: the named rows and the enumerations

name: W01 midDocumentMetadataBlocks: a new reader for every block
why: no answer changes, so cost tells it: each block reads from the top again, the quadratic spelling put back: the document rows at 8,000 blocks

name: W02 midDocumentMetadataBlocks: asks about the line after the block's opener
why: equivalent: the line asked about is the block's own `---` (three dashes and blanks, nothing else), which holds no marker, so reading one more line adds nothing

name: W03 midDocumentMetadataBlocks: a block outside the front matter is skipped only inside a comment
why: the front matter block is read as a mid-document block and a block in a comment is read: the existing qmd-model rows

name: W04 midDocumentMetadataBlocks: asks the comment question first
why: equivalent: a block that opens the document starts before or on the first content line, and every line above that is blank, so no marker is read and the cursor only moves on a little earlier

name: W05 midDocumentMetadataBlocks: the reader sees the lines from the first content line
why: a document that starts with blank lines and has a `<!--` in the block's own line: the cursor is handed lines shifted by the blank lines, reads the marker and refuses the block (the two- and three-blank-line rows)

name: W06 midDocumentMetadataBlocks: the reader sees the lines from the second line
why: every line number is one out: a comment opened on line 0 is never seen (the line-0 comment row)

name: H15 htmlCommentOpenAt: reads at most 100 lines further per question
why: a line asked 200, 1,500 or 150,000 lines below an opener nothing asked about before: the `lines above the line asked, asked first of all` rows, and the 1,500-line findHeadings row

name: H16 htmlCommentOpenAt: reads at most 1,000 lines further per question
why: the 1,500- and 150,000-line rows of `lines above the line asked`, and the findHeadings row with 1,500 blank lines between two blocks

name: H17 htmlCommentOpenAt: stops reading after 100,000 lines
why: the 150,000-line row of `lines above the line asked`: the opener is past the cap (the 200,000-line clock row opens at the start of each pair, so a cap does not move its count by itself)

name: H18 htmlCommentOpenAt: looks for a second marker only in the first 1,000 characters of a line
why: the 5,000-character line ending in a closed comment, asked on the next line: the closer is past the cap, so the comment stays open

name: H19 htmlCommentOpenAt: looks for a second marker only in the first 4,096 characters of a line
why: the same 5,000-character row

name: H20 htmlCommentOpenAt: a line indented four spaces holds no marker
why: the `opener indented by four spaces` and `closer indented by four spaces` named rows

name: H21 htmlCommentOpenAt: a tab-indented line holds no marker
why: the `opener indented by a tab` and `closer indented by a tab` named rows

name: H22 htmlCommentOpenAt: starts again only when the line is two before the cursor
why: `the line before the one it read to, by one`: asked 2 then 1 on [`<!--`, `-->`], the answer is true and this one answers the state after both lines

name: H23 htmlCommentOpenAt: a negative line never starts again
why: `a negative line after a read`: asked 1, -1, 1 on [`<!--`] the middle answer is false and this one keeps the open state

name: W07 midDocumentMetadataBlocks: the comment is asked only of a terminated block
why: the `closed by ...` row: quarto reads an unterminated block's content, so the comment is all that refuses it; the `...` outside a comment is its control

name: W08 midDocumentMetadataBlocks: a block one line below the first content line is skipped
why: the `block on the line right after the first line of content` row; the guard was there before Session 322 and no row stood on that line
